title: perf(canary): add regression detector and rollout hysteresis to canary guards
author: Jia Chen
release_notes: Add automated regression detection to perf canaries and introduce hysteresis-based rollout guards to avoid flip-flop in canary promotions. No user-facing API changes.
body:
Motivation: We observed intermittent canary flip-flops where transient latency spikes would roll back a canary and then immediate re-promotions would occur once the transient passed. This PR introduces a lightweight regression detector that flags statistically-significant latency/throughput regressions and adds hysteresis to the rollout guard so changes require sustained signal before automatic rollback/promotion.

What this PR does (single-string description):
- Implements an online regression detector that computes windowed percentiles and uses a paired-sample test against baseline canary windows to detect significant regressions (uses trimmed-mean + bootstrap for p-value approximation).
- Adds hysteresis parameters (detection_window, sustained_windows, cool_down) to the rollout guard so a single-window regression does not immediately trigger rollback.
- Exposes the guard tuning via canary config with safe defaults used in Hosted and Dedicated.
- Adds unit and integration tests that simulate noisy and persistent regressions.
- Adds a small benchmarks harness that runs controlled traffic to validate false-positive rate and detection latency.

Checklist: 
- [x] Regression detector implementation (perf-canary/detector.py and detector_test.go)
- [x] Hysteresis logic in rollout guard (rollout/guard.go)
- [x] Canary config updates + README (docs/perf-canary.md)
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Benchmarks and CI perf check added

Testing and evaluation:
- Local unit + integration: 100% pass.
- CI: added perf-canary-bench job that executes synthetic load across baseline and canary for 2 minutes; current patch recorded no false-positive regressions on canary-free baseline and detected 3/3 injected persistent regressions in test harness.
- Performance overhead: detector runs in <2ms per canary evaluation tick (~1s default tick) when evaluating 1000 requests across sliding windows.

Related: ENG-5234 (perf canary long-tail regressions), ENG-5342 (rollout stability improvements).

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Nice incremental design. A couple of notes: 1) default sustained_windows=3 seems aggressive for low-traffic routes, can we make it traffic-aware or expose lower default? 2) please add a comment on the statistical test choice and expected false-positive rate.

Jia Chen (author): Reply: Good catch — made sustained_windows configurable and added adaptive behavior: if request_per_minute < 100, sustained_windows falls back to 2. Also added doc section with test results showing ~2% false-positive under synthetic noise (see docs/perf-canary.md).
Rahul Singh: Requested changes: add an integration test that simulates transient spike followed by sustained regression to ensure rollbacks and promotions behave across back-to-back events.

Jia Chen: Added the integration test (rollout/guard_test.go) and verified locally. Test simulates transient spike + sustained regression and asserts single rollback for sustained case and no rollback for transient-only case.
Lydia Martinez: Approve after minor nits (typo in README and log level for detector should be debug by default). Jia addressed both. Approving.
